set.body:
Supporting track: Run. Track: engine and operations.

Acceptance
1. Unauthenticated liveness and readiness routes that reveal no detail. Readiness means the database and the blob store are reachable. The proxy and the container health check use them.
2. A nightly backup of the database and the blob store to the second disk, using the existing scripts, with a log line on success and a failure that someone sees.
3. One restore drill on a second machine or directory: restore last night's backup, sign in, open the pilot study, verify one file's digest, and confirm that a share revoked before the backup is still revoked. Record the recovery point, the elapsed time and the operator's steps.
4. The restore runbook closes the revocation gap. A plain restore brings back any access that was revoked after the backup. Either enrol the existing policy witness, which was built for this (docs/policy-witness.md, docs/organization-recovery.md), or keep a restored instance closed until every steward has re-checked their study's access list. Decide with the operator and write down which.
5. The drill is one script, so it can be repeated on demand. RUN5 repeats it on the pilot host.
6. A written emergency procedure for identifying data found in an accepted release: who decides, how the study is taken out of service at once, and how the bytes are removed. Lifecycle controls that do this inside the product (O04.1) are parked.
7. A two-page security overview for research IT and the privacy office: what is stored; who can sign in; how access is granted, explained and revoked; network exposure; backup and restore, including the choice made in step 4; and what is not yet done.

Not in scope
Metrics and alerting (O02.2), admission limits (O02.3), redacted diagnostics (the rest of O02.1) and automated off-host backup (O03.3). All parked.

Start from
- scripts/backup-postgres.sh, scripts/backup-store.py, scripts/restore-postgres.sh.
- docs/backup-bundle.md and docs/organization-recovery.md.
- modules/service/src/main/scala/sanctity/app/ApiServer.scala.

Evidence
A drill note here. The overview at docs/security-overview.md.
